The prompt asked for the percentage of screening conditions—excluding the no-T-cells control—with significant adjusted-p enrichment of immune-relevant pathways, written as a single number to /workspace/answer.txt [3], and both the hidden ground truth and reference solution specify 25% [4][5]. The agent ran a substantial analysis (RefSeq-to-symbol mapping, keyword tagging of 140 immune Reactome pathways, fold-change GSEA, MAGeCK −log10(p) GSEA, replicate-combined GSEA, and ORA) but ultimately wrote 0% [6][7]. Its ORA step fed gseapy every gene with MAGeCK p<0.05 (~1170 hits per replicate), which yielded zero adjusted-significant immune pathways in every column [8], and its replicate-combined GSEA summary likewise reported immune_sig_pos=0 for all five conditions (closest min immune FDR 0.155 for Chronic Round3) [9]. Treating these uniform nulls as conclusive across four methods, the agent declared 0% [10], but that conclusion depended on an ORA gene-selection choice (genome-wide p<0.05 cutoff and GSEA FDR across all 2,725 pathways) that washes out the focused hit-list signal; over-representation on a ranked top-hit gene set at the per-condition level recovers significant immune pathways in Chronic Round1 and therefore 25%, matching the benchmark answer [4][5]. The agent never tried that ranked-list ORA variant or reconciled its 0% against it, so it did not genuinely solve the task.

The hidden grader compared the submitted answer to the reference value 25% using exact percentage matching and scored reward 0.0 because the agent wrote 0% [1][2].
